speaker_role: student/recent applicant (YouTuber, not identified as counselor or AO)
commercial_incentive: None evident; standard YouTube subscribe/like requests only
key_insights: Freshman year grades count toward GPA, so treat it as 'round one' rather than a practice year, and use its relative ease to build a high GPA base
Try many clubs freshman year, then narrow to 1-3 that can be sustained all four years to show depth and genuine interest rather than resume padding
Meet with a guidance counselor early freshman year to map out a four-year course plan and avoid missing graduation requirements
Start a running document freshman year logging activities, achievements, and awards, since it becomes hard to track by senior year
Sophomore year should be used to explore potential academic interests and begin college research/campus visits before junior year gets too busy
Junior year is described as the most demanding: balancing coursework, standardized test prep, college list narrowing, scholarship deadlines, and starting a personal essay outline
In senior year, ask teachers and the counselor for recommendations within the first few weeks back at school to give them adequate time
FAFSA opens in October of senior year in the US and the speaker recommends filing early on a first-come, first-served assumption
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker states FAFSA opens in October (US) of senior year
notable_or_distinctive: A fairly generic year-by-year high school planning checklist from a personal YouTuber rather than a counselor; the FAFSA timing point is the only concrete external fact cited.
reliability_notes: Speaker admits uncertainty ('I don't remember exactly where in the timeline this is,' 'I'm clueless' about non-US aid systems); advice is personal opinion/anecdote, not sourced from admissions data, and largely generic.
